system.name: AD-LLM
system.one_liner: First benchmark of large language models for NLP anomaly detection, covering zero-shot detection, data augmentation and model selection.

content.variant_note: three colour-coded task cards on one shared LLM band, each with its input above the band and its output below
content.argues: LLMs can serve anomaly detection in three roles - as zero-shot detector with explanations, as data augmenter and as model selector - and the benchmark tests all three.
content.subject: Three NLP anomaly-detection tasks as input-to-output cards that share one LLM band.

content.reading_order: Starts at the LLM box on the left, then the three card titles left to right; inside each card top to bottom from input through the band to output.

layout.arrangement_note: Three rounded task cards side by side, each titled above, with a dashed grey LLM box on their left. One wide horizontal band crosses the cards at mid height and ends in a large arrowhead; every card puts its input above the band and its output below, joined by block arrows. The augmentation card is split into two sub-columns by a dashed line.
layout.lanes: three horizontal tiers shared by all cards: inputs above, the band in the middle, outputs below

style.stroke: 0.75 pt coloured outlines on the three rounded cards, 0.5-1 pt dashed frames and divider in grey, orange and green, 0.5 pt black chart axis
style.font: serif (CMU Serif), regular, 6.5 pt for titles and labels, 3-5 pt for the tiny snippets in the speech bubble
style.arrows: chunky outlined block arrows pointing down in the card colour; the band ends in a large arrowhead that fades out; thick plus signs join items
style.effects: soft gradient between the colour segments of the band and a fading arrowhead; otherwise none

encoding.color_means: one colour per task: blue = detection, orange = data augmentation, green = model selection, carried to the card tint, outline, band segment, block arrows and chart; grey = the LLM source
encoding.line_style_means: dashed grey frame = the LLM, dashed orange vertical line = split of the augmentation card into two sub-tasks, dashed green ellipse = the group of traditional AD models
encoding.shape_means: rounded card = one task; down block arrow = hand-over into or out of the band; plus sign = two things given or produced together; speech bubble = text read or written by the LLM
encoding.marker_means: TOP star = the recommended model; ellipses = the list goes on
encoding.emphasis: the single horizontal band shared by all cards makes the LLM the common engine, and the colour per task makes the three roles easy to tell apart
reusable_patterns: one horizontal gradient band running through all task cards to stand for the shared model
input above the band and output below it in every card, joined by block arrows

new_tags.what: one horizontal band running through all task cards for the model that serves every task, inputs above it and outputs below

lessons.what_to_learn: State several tasks of one model with a single shared band for the model and colour-coded cards that put each input above and each output below, so the figure reads as task definitions instead of architecture. Pair every input and output with a stock icon and a short caption, and use plus signs for composite outputs.
lessons.suits: Benchmark or study papers that test one model family on several tasks, where each task is an input-to-output definition.

evidence: AD-LLM examines how LLMs contribute to three key AD tasks
Our analysis focuses on three key tasks that are central in AD research and in practice (Figure 1)
LLMs generate synthetic samples and produce category descriptions to alleviate data scarcity and improve semantic reasoning

summary: AD-LLM is the first benchmark of how large language models help NLP anomaly detection. Figure 1 shows three colour-coded task cards over one shared horizontal band that stands for the LLM, whose source is a dashed box with a GPT-style logo and a llama on the left. Each card puts its input above the band and its output below: test data to AD scores plus an explanation; limited data and category names to synthetic data and category descriptions; traditional models, paper abstracts and dataset information to a top-selected model plus an explanation. Everything is drawn with small flat-colour stock icons, block arrows and plus signs on tinted rounded cards in serif type.
summary_zh: AD-LLM 是首个评测大模型做文本异常检测的基准。图1用三张按颜色区分的任务卡（零样本检测、数据增强、模型选择）共用一条代表LLM的横向色带，卡内上方为输入、下方为输出，配以扁平图标和加号。
notes: Prior primary kind contribution-mosaic reordered behind scope-overview because the cards map the tasks the benchmark covers; the band that runs through every card also makes it a fan-out pipeline, though the tasks are parallel and not sequential. The band is unlabelled; reading it as the LLM step rests on the logo box beside it and the arrows into and out of it.
